title: Attention Amnesia: When Chain-of-Thought Tuning Breaks Long-Range Recall
hook: Fine-tuning a hybrid LLM on chain-of-thought makes it reason better but quietly forget how to find a needle in a long haystack — and the fix is to just copy back two weight matrices.
key_points: Chain-of-thought supervised fine-tuning (CoT-SFT) systematically degrades long-context recall in hybrid linear-attention models like HypeNet and Jet-Nemotron.
On a 256K needle-in-a-haystack test, HypeNet-9B retrieval collapsed from 67.2% to 9.4% after CoT-SFT; the drop worsens with longer context.
Cause: CoT-SFT biases attention gradients toward short-range patterns, disrupting the W_Q/W_K projections that route long-range lookups.
QK-Restore is training-free: copy W_Q and W_K back from the pre-SFT checkpoint, keep everything else post-SFT — recovering recall while preserving reasoning.
content_html: Chain-of-thought (CoT) supervised fine-tuning is a standard way to boost reasoning. But the authors find it has a hidden cost in hybrid linear-attention models: it systematically degrades their long-context recall. Across architectures like HypeNet and Jet-Nemotron, needle-in-a-haystack (NIAH) retrieval deteriorates sharply after CoT-SFT, and the damage grows with harder retrieval settings and longer contexts — HypeNet-9B drops from 67.2% to 9.4% on a 256K test.
extra_html:
Diagnosis and fix

The authors trace the problem to gradients: CoT-SFT biases attention gradients toward short-range patterns, disrupting the query and key projections (W_Q, W_K) that are responsible for long-range routing. Their fix, QK-Restore, is training-free — restore only W_Q and W_K from the pre-SFT checkpoint while keeping every other post-SFT parameter. A Procrustes variant balances routing preservation against reasoning adaptation.

Why it matters

QK-Restore consistently recovers long-context capability at zero training cost while preserving reasoning gains — on HypeNet-5B it lifts S3@256K from 65.4% to 76.4%. The broader lesson: in hybrid architectures, reasoning and long-range retrieval can live in different parts of the weights, so a fine-tuning recipe that helps one can silently break the other.

related.title: Feature Learning in Gated Delta Networks at Scale
related.hook: muP lets you tune hyperparameters on a small model and transfer them to a huge one. This paper derives the equivalent rules for gated delta networks, so sub-quadratic models scale without re-tuning.

related.title: Ring Attention for Near-Infinite Context
related.hook: Spread one long sequence across many devices and compute attention blockwise - the context length you can handle grows with the number of devices, all with exact attention and no extra overhead.

prereqs.title: What Are State-Space Models?
prereqs.hook: A compact hidden state summarizes everything seen so far - update it with each new input and you get sequence modeling that scales linearly, not quadratically.
